The main takeaway from our work is that

H. pylori vacuolating toxin (VacA) upregulates the expression of chemokines in human eosinophil via Ca2+ and ROS-dependent NF-κB/IκB kinase (IκB) signaling pathways, which may play an important role in the pathogenesis of H. pylori infection.
